outcome: Delivery characteristics (gestational age at delivery, delivery timing, mode of delivery)
Neonatal complications (APGAR scores, cord pH, NICU admissions, respiratory distress, early neonatal deaths)
cohort: The study included 80 pregnant women at >36 weeks' gestation with pathological cerebroplacental ratio, equally divided into small-for-gestational-age (SGA) and adequate-for-gestational-age (AGA) groups based on estimated fetal weight.
finding: Pathological cerebroplacental ratio in SGA fetuses is associated with earlier delivery and poorer neonatal outcomes compared with AGA fetuses, despite similar management strategies.
mod_finding: Caesarean section due to fetal distress was significantly more common in the SGA group, while failed induction occurred more often in AGA fetuses.
birth_weight: SGA (<10th percentile) and AGA (>10th percentile) based on estimated fetal weight classification.
gest_age: Enrollment occurred at >36 weeks' gestation; deliveries ranged from 37.68 to 38.3 weeks' gestation.
